author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Set up two local PS2 controllers
summary: Build Port 2 from a known-good two-player baseline, test each controller alone and together, and prove device order remains correct after disconnecting both pads.
heroAlt: OnePad configuration comparison representing separate mappings for two local PS2 controller ports

sourceLabels.pcsx2-controllers-current: PCSX2 mappings, profiles, ports, and peripherals

blocks.text: Prove port isolation before starting multiplayer
Assign two physical devices to separate PS2 ports without allowing either device to feed both players.
Automatic mapping can append the second pad to Port 1 instead of creating an isolated Port 2 assignment.
Name both devices and preserve Player 1

items: Two controllers charged and visible under distinct Android device names.
Port 1 already passes a complete single-player test.
A genuine two-player PS2 mode available without multitap.

blocks.text: Map and challenge one port at a time

items: 1. Connect only the intended Player 1 pad and confirm the existing Port 1 map.
2. Connect Player 2 and create a separately named Port 2 mapping.
3. Inspect Port 1 for entries from the second device and remove accidental additions.
4. With Player 1 untouched, test every essential Player 2 control.
5. With Player 2 untouched, repeat the isolation check for Player 1.
6. Press different directions simultaneously and confirm the game separates both players.
7. Disconnect both devices, reconnect Player 2 first, then Player 1.
8. Cold-launch the two-player mode and verify that physical roles did not swap.

blocks.text: Testing each controller alone reveals cross-port bindings that remain hidden when both players press buttons together.
Player 1 and Player 2 respond only to their assigned devices and keep their roles after a cold reconnect.

items: Each pad controls exactly one PS2 port.
Menus and gameplay agree about Player 1 and Player 2.
Both pads move Player 1: remove Player 2 codes from Port 1 before remapping Port 2.
Player 2 works only in menus: confirm the title's actual multiplayer mode and expected port.
Roles swap after reconnect: follow stable controller-order diagnosis.
More than two players are expected: verify the title's multitap port and slot rules.

blocks.text: Return to the proven single-pad arrangement
Restore the single-player Port 1 profile and clear only the newly created Port 2 experiment.
Two players and multitap are different configurations
A normal two-controller title uses the console's two base ports; games for three or more players may require a specific multitap port and slot order.
Read PCSX2 port and multitap documentation
